Jules: Hey folks — built a quick closet booth for calls using an IKEA wardrobe + moving blankets + a duvet. Not pretty but cuts echo a ton. Anyone tried something similar? Tips for airflow & not melting in summer? pic: [img]
Sam: omg love the duvet trick. For airflow I cut small vents at the top and used a clip-on fan pointing out. don't tape things to the walls though, they trap heat. :sweat_smile:
Priya: If you care about voice clarity, get a cheap foam mic shield + pop filter. Also enable Noise Suppression in Meet/Zoom or use Krisp. On Linux I run pulse + rnnoise — big win.
infra-bot: heads-up: closet booths are 87% more likely to trigger curiosity from roommates. :robot_face:
Lena: pro tip — a USB desk fan on low, clipped to a shelf, keeps air moving without making a weird drone if you point it away from the mic. Add a small silica packet if you're worried about damp duvet smell.
Mark: For recordings, treat it like a vocal booth: absorption at reflection points (opposite wall, ceiling). Bass is tough in a small closet — avoid mixing with a big subwoofer. Also monitor temps if you shove a PC in there.
Aisha: I jury-rigged a $30 laptop cooling pad standing under my monitor stand, pushed air out through the closet gap. Saved me on longer calls. :thumbsup:
Kris: Also consider a dynamic mic (e.g., Shure SM58/SM7) — they reject room noise more than condensers if you're not doing professional recordings.
Jules: Thanks all! Going to try fan-out + foam shield tonight and enable Krisp. Will report back with before/after audio clip.
Priya: quick Linux trick if someone's snoozing on background hum: run `pactl list sources` and then `pactl set-source-mute <id> 1` for the offending loopback. YMMV but useful for weird hardware hums.
Sam: photos or it didn't happen :camera_with_flash:
Jules: will post pics + a tiny audio sample tomorrow. Appreciate the pointers! :blush:
